correctness.rationale: The proof distinguishes all pair types. With \(S=\sum_P\binom{d_P}{2}\), \(J=\sum_\pi\binom{y_\pi}{2}\), and \(D\) the number of doubled geometric lines, exact pair accounting gives \(J=S+4D\). For \(34\) line copies, convexity of point degrees forces \(S\ge120\), while \(238\) line-plane incidences with plane occupancy at most two force \(J\le119\), contradiction. For \(33\) copies, one doubled line forces three degree-two points and then \(S\ge114\), so \(J\ge118>115\); hence any \(33\)-configuration is simple. The remaining \(111\le S\le115\) interval gives the five stated plane spectra. The bundled verifier reconstructs all relevant incidences and checks an explicit \(32\)-line witness.

value.rationale: This is the first small binary line-plane parameter highlighted by the recent source, whose published value has a two-unit uncertainty and whose upper analysis uses ILP. The result removes the value 34 by a short theoretical certificate, reducing the problem to the single existence question 32 versus 33. It additionally proves that every possible 33-line extremizer is simple and has one of only five plane spectra, giving concrete structure for the remaining classification/search problem. The contribution is therefore not a routine recomputation of the known 32-line witness.
